status: Pilot, written by Claude on 12 November 2026 and not yet checked by the translation workers. Vocabulary follows the course: autobus, voiture.

lessons.title: Sounds and Script - Silent Last Letters, Part 1
lessons.description: The last consonant of a French word is usually written and not said. Listen for what is missing in petit, grand, Paris, and beaucoup.

lessons.title: Sounds and Script - Nasal Vowels, Part 1
lessons.description: Before an n or an m, the vowel is said through the nose and the n itself is not said. Hear vin, vent, bon, and pain.

lessons.title: Sounds and Script - The French U, Part 1
lessons.description: French has two sounds where English has one: the ou of vous, and the tighter u of tu. Hear tout against tu, and vous against vu.

lessons.title: Sounds and Script - Accent Marks, Part 1
lessons.description: An accent mark can be the only thing that tells two words apart. Compare ou with où, and a with à.

lessons.title: Patterns - To Go in the Present, Part 1
lessons.description: The verb aller, to go, changes to say who is going. Spot what changes: vais, vas, va, allons.

lessons.title: Patterns - To Go in the Present, Part 2
lessons.description: More of aller, to go: for all of you, for them, for "let's", and for what you are about to do.

lessons.title: Patterns - More Than One, Part 1
lessons.description: For more than one, the word gains an s that is written and not said, and le or la becomes les. It is les that you hear.

lessons.title: Patterns - Words That Match, Part 1
lessons.description: A describing word matches the thing it describes: petit with le garçon, petite with la fille. The added e brings the silent last letter back to life.

lessons.title: Sentence Building - Asking a Question, Part 1
lessons.description: Put est-ce que in front of a statement and it becomes a question. Nothing else moves.
words: This is the bus to Paris.
Is this the bus to Paris?
Est-ce que c'est l'autobus pour Paris ?

lessons.title: Sentence Building - Saying No, Part 1
lessons.description: No takes two words in French, one on each side of the verb: ne before it, and pas after it.

lessons.title: Sentence Building - Describing Words Come After, Part 1
lessons.description: In English the describing word comes first: a white house. In French it usually comes after: une maison blanche.

lessons.title: Sentence Building - A Few Describing Words Come First, Part 1
lessons.description: A handful of everyday describing words, for size, goodness, and beauty, come before the thing instead of after it.

lessons.title: Sentences in Use - Going Places, Part 1
lessons.description: The verb aller, to go, at work in whole sentences. Spot vais, allons, vas, and vont.
words: I am going to the market.
We are going to the beach.
Are you going to the party?
Est-ce que tu vas à la fête ?

lessons.title: Sentences in Use - Questions and Answers, Part 1
lessons.description: A question and its answer, side by side. The answer drops est-ce que, and a no adds ne and pas.
words: Est-ce que tu as une voiture ?
No, I do not speak English.
Non, je ne parle pas anglais.

lessons.title: Sentences in Use - Describing Things, Part 1
lessons.description: Describing words matching what they describe, in whole sentences: blanche, rouges, grande, petits.

lessons.title: Sentences in Use - Yesterday, Today, and Tomorrow, Part 1
lessons.description: One trip to the market, told three ways: already done, happening now, and still to come.
words: I went to the market yesterday.
Hier, je suis allé au marché.
I am going to the market today.
I will go to the market tomorrow.
I am going to go tomorrow.
